1 tablespoon cumin
4 cups vegetable broth, divided
1 small onion, diced
1 large green pepper, diced
2 cloves garlic, minced
1 small sweet potato, peeled and diced
1 tablespoon olive oil
3 cans dark red kidney beans, drained and rinsed
3/4 cup dry quinoa, rinsed
1/2 cup light coconut milk
1-28 ounce can crushed tomatoes
Salt and pepper, to taste
Sliced green onions, for serving
Plain Greek yogurt, for serving
description: A big batch of chili brings to mind tailgating parties and state fair cookoffs, but the truth is, chili can be one heck of a clean eating rock star. This version is full of veggies, whole grains, lean protein and complex carbs. The Thai flavors of this dish add a special delicious dash of interest.

name: Velvety Potato Soup
ingredients:
2 slices of bacon
1 tablespoon butter
Pinch of red pepper flakes
2 garlic cloves, minced
2 medium onions, diced
3 stalks of celery, diced
3 pounds of potatoes, peeled and diced (about 6 medium)
6 cups chicken or vegetable stock
1-1/2 cups skim milk
2 bay leaves
1/2 teaspoon dried thyme
Salt and pepper, to taste
1 cup low-fat Greek yogurt
Cheddar cheese, sliced green onions, etc. for topping
description: This healthier version of the calorie and fat-laden classic is still creamy and flavorful thanks the addition of low-calorie, high-protein Greek yogurt.

name: Watermelon Feta Salad
ingredients:
3 cups lettuce mix
3 cups bite-sized watermelon chunks
1/2 cup halved Kalamata olives
4 ounces crumbled feta cheese
1 medium cucumber, sliced
, for serving

name: Wedding Cauliflower Soup
ingredients:
1 tbsp. olive oil
1 tbsp. butter
1 small onion, diced
1 medium carrot, diced
2 medium stalks celery, diced
1 clove garlic, minced
3-4 tbsp. fresh parsley, chopped
1 head cauliflower, roughly chopped
4 c. broth (chicken or veggie)
3/4 c. half and half
1/4 c. sour cream
Salt and pepper

name: White Bean Chicken Chili
ingredients:
1 tbsp. olive oil
1 medium onion, diced
3 cloves garlic, minced
2 cans diced green chiles
2 large chicken breasts (around 1 lb.) cooked and shredded
4 c. chicken broth
2 cans great northern beans, drained and rinsed
1 tbsp. cumin
1 tbsp. chili powder
1 tsp. oregano
Salt and pepper to taste

name: White Zombie (AKA : White Chocolate Mocha)
ingredients:
3 ounces white chocolate
1/2 c. half and half cream (can substitute any kind of milk)
12 ounces strongly brewed coffee
Cinnamon

name: Whole Grain Bagels
ingredients:
5 cups whole wheat flour
1 cup old-fashioned oats
2-1/2 tablespoons yeast
5 tablespoons sugar
2 tablespoons kosher salt
3-1/2 cups hot water
2 cups white flour
1 tablespoon olive oil
3 quarts water
2 tablespoons brown rice syrup (optional, helps shine up the bagels)
1 egg white, beaten with 1 tablespoon water

name: Whole Grain Butterscotch Bars
ingredients:
6 tablespoons butter, melted
1 cup packed brown sugar
1 egg, lightly beaten
1 teaspoon vanilla
2 1/2 cups oats
2 cups whole wheat flour
1/2 teaspoon salt
1/2 teaspoon baking soda
1-14 ounce can fat-free sweetened condensed milk
1 1/2 cups butterscotch chips
description: I made the mistake of baking these in a baking pan without parchment paper. Do as I say, not as I do. The butterscotch becomes caramelized and sticky after baking and can make pan clean-up a nightmare. Protect your pan (and your sanity) with a layer of parchment paper.

name: Whole Grain Carrot Cake Whoopie Pies
ingredients:
1 cup whole wheat flour
1/2 cup all-purpose flour
1/2 cup oats
1 teaspoon baking powder
1 teaspoon cinnamon
1/4 teaspoon nutmeg
Pinch of salt
1/4 cup pure pumpkin puree
1/4 cup butter, melted
1/2 cup packed brown sugar
1/2 cup sugar
2 eggs
1 teaspoon vanilla extract
1-1/2 cup shredded carrots
8 ounces of cream cheese, softened
1 cup confectioner's sugar
Pinch of salt
1/2 teaspoon vanilla extract
description: There is something nice about the simplicity of the two cookies filled with the winter white frosting, but for a bit of texture and fun decor, feel free to roll the whoopies in crushed walnuts or flaked coconut.

name: Whole Grain Pancake Mix
ingredients:
3 1/2 cups old-fashioned oats
4 cups whole wheat flour
1 cup all-purpose flour
3 tablespoons sugar
3 tablespoons baking powder

1 tablespoon baking soda
1 cup vegetable oil

name: Whole Wheat Coconut Tortillas
ingredients:
2-2/3 cups whole wheat flour, divided
1 teaspoon sea salt
1/3 cup coconut oil
1 cup hot water
description: These guilt-free tortillas are packed full of whole grains and healthy fats—all with a super short ingredient list. The coconut oil adds a really nice light, sweet coconut flavor that works beautifully with savor and sweet fillings.

name: Whole Wheat Cottage Cheese Pancakes
ingredients:
1 1/4 cup whole wheat bread flour
1 teaspoon baking powder
1/2 teaspoon ground cinnamon
1/4 teaspoon ground nutmeg
1/4 teaspoon kosher salt

1/2 cup unsweetened applesauce

1/2 teaspoon vanilla extract
Cooking spray
description: These fluffy pancakes will fool even the biggest whole grain hater. Babyface took one bite of these and said, "Do these have any whole wheat flour in them at all?" Yes, they certainly do!

2-1/2 teaspoons active dry yeast (1 packet)

1 tablespoon sugar
1-1/2 cup whole wheat flour
1 cup all-purpose flour
5 tablespoons olive oil, divided
1-1/2 teaspoons kosher salt, divided
2 teaspoons minced garlic
3 tablespoons melted butter
1/4 cup finely chopped parsley
description: To get the eight knots, I made mine pretty hefty in size. Feel free to size them down to make mini versions and make this recipe stretch to feed a lot more hungry mouths.

name: Whole Wheat Lemon Poppy Seed Scones
ingredients:
2 cups whole wheat flour (plus more for forming)
1/3 cup packed brown sugar
2 teaspoons baking powder
1/8 teaspoon kosher salt
1 stick butter, cut into small pieces and chilled
2 eggs
1 teaspoon vanilla
1/2 cup + 1 tablespoon milk, divided
2 lemons
1 tablespoon poppy seeds
1/2-1 cup powdered sugar

name: Whole Wheat Naan
ingredients:
1/4 cup warm skim milk
2 1/4 t. yeast (or one packet)
2 1/2 cups whole wheat flour
1/2 cup all-purpose flour
1 cup plain, low fat yogurt
1/2 T. sugar
1/4 t. baking powder
1 t. salt
2 T. Olive Oil
Seasoning for top (we used garlic salt)
description: Whole wheat, chewy and delicious! Pair these with your favorite Indian food.

name: Whole Wheat Pizza Crust
ingredients:

3 tbsp. olive oil
1 tbsp. sugar
1 tsp. salt
2 c. whole wheat flour
1 c. white flour

2 1/2 tsp. yeast (1 packet)
1 tbsp. basil

name: Wild Blueberry Banana Super Bread with Lemon Glaze

1 ripe banana, mashed
3/4 cup ground flaxseed
2 egg whites (about 1/4 cup liquid)

Cooking spray

ingredients:
2 pounds small Yukon Gold potatoes, quartered
1 1/2 teaspoon Kosher salt, divided

3/4 cups lowfat Greek yogurt

Ice

Nonfat milk

description: We serve this festive drink in old-fashioned glasses, but if you are throwing a party, it might be fun to toss it into a shaker with ice and then strain it into martini glasses for your guests.

3 potatoes, sliced thinly
1 cup half and half

name: lazy pizza dough + favorite margherita pizza
ingredients:
3 cups (375 grams) all-purpose flour (bread flour works too)
Slightly heaped 1/8, 1/4 or 1/2 teaspoon active dry yeast (for
,
, or
respectively, above)
1 1/2 teaspoons sea or kosher salt
1 1/4 cup water, plus an additional tablespoon or two if needed (updated)
2 12-inch round or 9×13 rectangular pizza doughs
1 28-ounce can whole peeled tomatoes
1 clove garlic, minced
1/2 teaspoon sea or kosher salt
Red pepper flakes, to taste
Pinch of sugar, if desired
8 ounces aged mozzarella (sold in plastic, not water) (use more if you like your pizza with extra cheese)
1/4 cup finely grated parmesan or pecorino romano cheese
Two glugs of olive oil
Few leaves of fresh basil, torn or sliced
description: Raise your hand if you never get pizza right when you make it at home — that the dough doesn’t rise in the time the recipe says it should or it’s impossible to roll out; or that you get it rolled out but once baked, it tastes less like a good pizza crust and more like a tough cracker. Or maybe the opposite happens, that it’s so thick and bready, it reminds you more of a bagel, and sadly, not in a good way. Raise your hand if it never resembles the stuff from you favorite wood-wired pizzeria, all bubbled and crisp but stretchy within, with charred spots throughout and slices that don’t flop like overcooked spaghetti once lifted, sauce and cheese sliding away from you just when you need them in your mouth the most.

name: Slow Cooker Caramelized Apples
ingredients:
8 cups Diced Peeled Baking Apples
1 cup Dark Brown Sugar
4 Tablespoons Unsalted Butter, melted
1 Tablespoon Ground Cinnamon
½ teaspoons Kosher Salt
1 dash Freshly Grated Nutmeg
2 teaspoons Pure Vanilla Extract
description: All the flavor of apple pie filling with none of the fuss making and rolling out the crust.

name: Smoked Salmon Salad

1 pound Smoked Salmon, Wild

¼ cups Ponzu Sauce
description: This salad works for any occasion. You can bring it to work for lunch or take it to a fancy dinner party. It is beautiful when layered in a platter, an Asian dish or in a clear glass bowl.

name: Pumpkin Pie Hummus

15 ounces, weight Canned Chickpeas/garbanzo Beans

description: A sweet, healthy, vegan, gluten-free dip made with pumpkin, maple syrup and spices. It tastes just like pumpkin pie!

name: Mexican Chicken Salad

1 head (Small Head) Romaine Lettuce, Torn Into Pieces

description: Mexican Chicken Salad is so easy and so full of flavor!

name: My “I Challenge All Claims to the Ultimate Brine” Turkey Brine
ingredients:
20 cups (20 Cups Is 5 Litres Or 1.25 Gallons) Cold Water
1 cup Fine Salt

2 heads Of Garlic, Sliced In Half (Leave The Skin On)
1 whole (Large) Onion, Sliced In Quarters

description: I’ve always claimed to roast the best turkey in the world but with this brine; I’m totally right.  Modest-shmodest; you have to try this recipe, it’s insane!

name: Roasted Vegetable Pasta Sauce

3 stalks Celery, Cut Into 1" Pieces

4 ounces, weight Canned Pumpkin (not Pumpkin Pie Filling)
1 whole Egg
2 teaspoons Maple Syrup
description: Eat one with coffee. Eat one slathered in butter. Eat three for breakfast.

name: Pumpkin Bacon Polenta
ingredients:
8 slices Bacon
4 cups Water
2 cups Chicken Broth
1 cup Canned 100% Pure Pumpkin Puree

¼ teaspoons Cinnamon
⅛ teaspoons Nutmeg
1 teaspoon Salt
½ teaspoons Pepper

½ cups Heavy Cream

ingredients:
4 cups Water, Divided Use
1 cube Beef Bouillon
1 whole White Onion, Diced
2 cups Green Bell Peppers, Chopped

2 teaspoons Crushed Red Pepper Flakes
1 Tablespoon Garlic Salt
¼ cups Seasoned Bread Crumbs
2 cups Tomato Sauce

name: Chipotle Artichoke Hummus

30 ounces, weight Canned Garbanzo Beans, Rinsed And Drained
2 whole Chipotle Peppers In Adobo Sauce

name: Caramelized Apples in the Crockpot

1-½ pound Apples (1 1/2 Pounds Is Roughly 5 1/2 Large Apples), Cored And Sliced

2 teaspoons Cinnamon, Ground

1 cup Cold Milk
1 box Vanilla Pudding Mix (3.4 Oz Package)

name: Apple Butternut Squash Soup with Rosemary & Chipotle
ingredients:
2-½ pounds Butternut Squash (2 1/2 Pounds Is Roughly 1 Medium Sized Squash)
1 whole Large Apple, Cored And Roughly Chopped (recommend Honeycrisp)
1 whole Medium Yellow Onion, Peeled And Quartered

¼ cups All-purpose Flour
1 pound Beef (Round Roast) Cubes

4 cups Beef Stock (canned Is Fine)
1 whole Onion, Peeled And Diced
3 whole Carrots, Peeled And Sliced
4 cloves Garlic, Peeled And Minced

3 Tablespoons FOR THE FILLING:
1 Tablespoon Minced Fresh Cilantro
1 Tablespoon Minced Fresh Basil
1 Tablespoon Minced Fresh Rosemary

Thanks to the fresh herbs and Parmesan cheese, it has tons of flavor but it’s light on calories and fat. In under an hour, you can have a crave-worthy meal that will please the entire family.

name: Peanut Butter Chocolate Banana Bread
ingredients:
1 cup Granulated Sugar

1 carton Vegetable Broth (1 Liter Carton)
1 cup Chopped Pak Choi (Chinese Cabbage)
3 ounces, weight Rice Noodles
description: Who said comfort foods have to be unhealthy? Here’s my version of the Vietnamese Pho Bo.

name: Burger-Stuffed Baked Potatoes
ingredients:
1 Tablespoon Olive Oil
⅔ pounds Ground Beef
4 whole Salt And Pepper, to taste
description: It’s a burger in a potato, guys.  Just stop fighting it.

description: Most homemade caramel popcorn uses corn syrup, which I’m not completely adverse to. But let’s face it, if you can use something better than that, why not? I use honey along with apple juice, apple chips and a touch of brown sugar. A dash of cinnamon brings the apple forward, but if you really want to make the popcorn extra apple-y, just crush another 1/2 cup of apple chips into a powder by using a spice grinder, coffee grinder, mortar and pestle or plain old ziplock bag and rolling pin. Once you have the apple powder stir it into the caramel before you pour it over the popcorn.

description: In one of my favorite October traditions, we picked too many apples a few weekends ago. As in maybe perhaps 25 pounds more than we needed? It’s hard to gauge. I realize that if you’ve never been in an apple orchard in October, when you’ve escaped the city to find yourselves in a quiet grove as the leaves are just starting to turn and the sky is unimaginably blue and you’re wearing your first thick sweater of the season, it’s hard to imagine how one accidentally picks 25 pounds too many apples. But I bet if you’ve been there and felt that, how fun it is to pluck crisp, unblemished, unwaxed apples from trees and let the branches snap back and the leaves flutter droplets of last night’s rain over your face, you’ve probably gotten carried away . I think picking too many apples in October is about as important of a tradition as burning food on a backyard grill over July 4th weekend and going through a whole jar of cinnamon every fall. It’s going to happen either way; it’s best to embrace it.

The secret to making easy caramel apples is the microwave. Yep, you can make caramel sauce by microwaving sugar, water and a little corn syrup together. It’s painless and the microwave does all the work for you. One thing to note, don’t try this method with organic sugar. You have to use plain old regular refined white sugar. Chess pie is similar to vinegar, sugar or custard pies with the addition of a little cornmeal to give it texture. Stories range on why it’s called chess pie. Some say it’s a bastardization of the age old question “What sort of pie is that?” The response of “it’s just pie” slowly morphing into “it’s chess pie.” Other people say it’s an evolution of storing the warm pies in a pie chest, a specific piece of furniture popular in the south that is used to cool pies (man I wish I lived in a culture where there were specific pieces of furniture designed just to cool cakes and pies!). The resulting cooling pie was a “chest pie”, or “chess pie” as the phrase evolved. Either way though, the simple and easy to variation of pumpkin pie is a familiar but slightly different dessert, perfect for Thanksgiving.

Chess pie is similar to vinegar, sugar or custard pies with the addition of a little cornmeal to give it texture. Stories range on why it’s called chess pie. Some say it’s a bastardization of the age old question “What sort of pie is that?” The response of “it’s just pie” slowly morphing into “it’s chess pie.” Other people say it’s an evolution of storing the warm pies in a pie chest, a specific piece of furniture popular in the south that is used to cool pies (man I wish I lived in a culture where there were specific pieces of furniture designed just to cool cakes and pies!). The resulting cooling pie was a “chest pie”, or “chess pie” as the phrase evolved. Either way though, the simple and easy to variation of pumpkin pie is a familiar but slightly different dessert, perfect for Thanksgiving.

description: The trick to making these ridiculously easy homemade potato chips is to use Yukon gold potatoes. Don’t try it with Idaho russets or Red potatoes. Any oil will do, but I prefer rice bran or peanut oil because of the high smoke point. Bonus if you feel like adding a couple of tablespoons of bacon fat into the oil, to give the chips a subtle savoriness, but that’s not super necessary.

And although I realize there is barely a page on the internet or of printed matter near you right now not currently angling to be the one that gets to walk you through the biggest home cooking holiday of the year next week, I like this one more. Maybe it’s because one of the earliest lines in the book is “You can go your whole life and then wake up one morning and look in the refrigerator at this animal carcass the size of a toddler and think: . name: parsley leaf potatoes
ingredients:
In November 2003, Gourmet Magazine published a recipe for Parsley-Leaf Potatoes that have rarely gotten half the spotlight they deserve. No purple majesty, tri-colored miniature or even Yukon gold potatoes are enlisted to make these potatoes, just the Russets that most of this country simply calls “potatoes.” You’re not going to need extra virgin olive oil or goose fat, single-origin sea salt, shallots, minced herbs, lemon, mustard or self-enclosed packets of soft roasted garlic. There isn’t even any freshly ground black pepper. There is only salt and parsley leaves that are pressed flat against cut potato halves that roast in the puddle of melted butter for the better part of an hour until they are flipped over into a serving dish, the leaves and potato edges now crisp, golden and ready for a magazine cover. (Um, yours will be. I used my oldest, crustiest pan and mine look like, aptly, they’re ready for … this blog.
someone who made them look prettier.)
3 ounces (6 tablespoons) unsalted butter
8 small-medium baking potatoes (about 4 pounds), scrubbed

Coarse salt
description: As you may have noticed, as the week’s progressed, things have gotten simpler. We started with great ambitions  — we will make a   We will trim the beans! make a roux! sauté the mushrooms! coat and deep-fry the onions! We moved onto my  made from torn baguettes, diced apples and onions and celery, three herbs, sometimes cornbread, sometimes sausage; it’s a two-pan ordeal. We slipped quietly into the simple weeknight savior, . At the rate we’re going, I’ll have a boiled water recipe on the site by Monday. But somewhere between five-ingredient breadcrumbs and recipes that don’t need to be spelled out, there’s this, a potato recipe with only salt, butter and parsley.

2 Tablespoons Fresh Cranberries For Garnish
1 bunch Fresh Mint For Garnish
description: Simple, festive and very refreshing!

name: Sweet and Savory Pumpkin Dip
ingredients:
8 ounces, weight Light Cream Cheese
½ cups Canned Pumpkin Puree
½ cups Norwegian Brown Cheese, Grated
3 whole Green Onions, Sliced
¼ cups Pecans, Chopped
½ teaspoons Seasoned Salt
¼ teaspoons Cinnamon
½ cups Pomegranate Seeds, For Garnish
description: Slightly sweet and savory and perfect for pre-holiday noshing.

name: Quinoa Pilaf with Green Apples, Dried Cranberries and Pecans
ingredients:
1 cup White Quinoa
1-½ cup Red Quinoa
4 cups Vegetable Stock
¼ cups Olive Oil
½ whole Red Onion, Diced
2 stalks Celery, Diced
1 clove Garlic, Minced
1-½ teaspoon Herbes De Provence
1 teaspoon Salt
2 whole Black Pepper To Taste
½ cups Green Apples, Diced (Skin On)
1 cup Dry White Wine
1 cup Dried Cranberries
¼ cups Toasted Or Maple Pecans
description: In this recipe I’ve used classic Thanksgiving flavors like apples and cranberries with quinoa, which may not be that familiar as a Thanksgiving ingredient but I think this mix of these ingredients will become an instant classic.

name: Oven Roasted Brussels Sprouts
ingredients:
2 pounds Brussels Sprouts
¼ cups Extra Virgin Olive Oil
2 Tablespoons Balsamic Vinegar
½ teaspoons Salt
description: This is my favorite way to prepare Brussels sprouts; they get caramelized and the outer leaves get crispy. You’ll never boil them again.

name: Thanksgiving Bites over Fresh Cranberry Sauce
ingredients:
1 pound FOR THE MEATBALLS:
2 whole Ground Chicken
½ whole Apples
5 leaves White Onion
1 whole Sage
½ cups Egg
1 cup Applesauce
1 teaspoon Italian Breadcrumbs
3 cups Salt
1 cup FOR THE CRANBERRY SAUCE:
¾ cups Fresh Cranberries
description: These chicken meatballs with apples and sage are served over fresh cranberry sauce and taste just  like Thanksgiving in a bite, hence the name. They are the perfect prelude to Turkey Day! They’re great to serve guests over this weekend or the night before Thanksgiving. On the other hand, if you want to bypass all of the fuss, you could try serving these meatballs to your Thanksgiving guests.

name: Kimchi “Pizza Rolls”
ingredients:
2 cups FOR THE PIZZA ROLLS:
2 cups Shredded Monterrey Jack
3 Tablespoons Drained And Finely Chopped Kimchi
50 pieces Sour Cream
2 Tablespoons Wonton Wrappers (recommended: Nasoya Brand)
1 Tablespoon Vegetable Oil, For Frying
2 Tablespoons Cornstarch, For Dusting
1 pinch FOR THE CILANTRO-LIME MAYO:
1 Tablespoon Chopped Cilantro
description: Store bought wonton wrappers make for excellent homemade pizza rolls. These are filled with chopped kimchi and shredded Monterey jack and served with cilantro lime mayo. The method would work for traditional cheese and tomato-filled pizza rolls, too.

name: Maple Pumpkin Fudge
ingredients:
1 can FOR THE FUDGE:
1-⅔ cup 5 Oz. Can Evaporated Milk
½ teaspoons Brown Sugar
24 whole Salt
2 cups Jet-Puffed Pumpkin Spice Marshmallows
3 Tablespoons White Chocolate Chips
1 Tablespoon Canned Pumpkin Puree
½ teaspoons Pure Maple Syrup
¼ teaspoons Maple Essence/extract
1 cup Pumpkin Pie Spice
¼ teaspoons FOR THE TOPPING:
description: Pumpkin fudge sweetened with pure maple syrup and topped with bittersweet chocolate and sea salt.

name: Corn ‘n Ham Cheese Casserole
ingredients:
2 Tablespoons Margarine
1 whole Large Onion, Finely Chopped
5 cloves Garlic, Minced
½ teaspoons Salt
3 cans 15 3/4 Ounce Cans, Corn Kernels, Drained
1 cup Heavy Cream
1 cup Milk
8 ounces, weight Cream Cheese
1 cup Shredded Swiss Cheese
1 cup Shredded Sharp Cheddar Cheese
1 pound Chopped Ham
½ cups Yellow Cornmeal
3 Tablespoons Flour
description: This is a hearty casserole that could also be served in smaller portions as a side dish this holiday season.  Or use your leftover ham from a holiday meal! If your diet restricts ham substitute chicken or tuna and enjoy in your own way!

name: White Lasagna with Roasted Brussels Sprouts and Cauliflower
ingredients:
4 cups Fresh Brussels Sprouts
1 head Cauliflower
1 Tablespoon Olive Oil
1 teaspoon Balsamic Vinegar
1 pinch Coarse Salt
3 Tablespoons Unsalted Butter
¼ cups Shallots, Minced
4 cloves Garlic, Peeled And Minced
⅓ cups All-purpose Flour
2 cups Low Sodium Chicken Broth
1-½ cup Half-and-half
1 teaspoon Coarse Salt
1 pinch Nutmeg
12  No Boil Lasagna Noodles
10 ounces, weight Fontina Cheese, Shredded
4 ounces, weight Parmesan Cheese, Shredded
⅓ cups Pine Nuts
description: Cheesy, creamy white lasagna filled with roasted Brussels sprouts and cauliflower.
